A10 and C2 were already done on master: one atsRating(template, settings) feeds the picker badge and the ATS Check (TUI-5 / R2-011, pinned by 69-picker-ats-badge), and each dashboard card names its template (b7a5e21, R2-133). Now (A6): each template card says what its engine draws and makes no ATS claim in words. The badge makes that claim, from atsRating. Classic no longer claims a 'Two-column header'. Executive names its role-first entries on one line. The Sidebar card names the page its Layout prints. (A5): one line under the picker says what a switch keeps and what it changes. A test runs every pair of templates and checks that a switch changes only the settings that line names. The cards carry data-testid="template-<id>", and the Cypress specs pick templates by it rather than by the old descriptions.

rows.summary: B1 shipped. Design → Template now offers 17 choices: the 9 templates plus 8 designs. The designs are Harbor, Ledger, Nordic, Crimson, Midnight, Sunrise, Grove and Inkwell. Each one is a named look over an existing engine: its own font and accent, plus a heading style, header and spacing (src/constants/templatePresets.js). A design is picked through the store's setTemplate(engine, preset), using the same switch the parity walker uses (withTemplate). It is stored as settings.templatePreset, and the picker marks its card. Picking a plain template takes the design's look away wherever the user kept it. Reset returns to the design. JSON Resume writes it as meta.design and imports it back; Backup keeps it. It never writes a section's own settings. Every design passes the ATS field battery on pdf.js and every Poppler mode (42-ats-fields). Its badge is atsRating over its engine and settings. Its name and job title read on its header. Its values stay inside the panel's ranges. The parity registry measures the new control: a design picked prints what a résumé started on it prints, unlike its engine, and its accent prints. Word prints the designs' fonts and accents. With no design set, everything prints as before.
rows.remaining: B2: new layout code (the ten designed layouts). B4: save my own design. A preset-keyed entry layout (resolveSection) was not built, because designs deliberately leave section settings alone. The dashboard card and the cover-letter panel name the design's template, not the design.

issues: Stale comment in templatePresets.js named test files that do not exist. Real; fixed in c2eff4d.
Crimson's description says 'Gelasio serif' (the font that prints) while the Typography menu shows 'Georgia'. Wording only; left as it is.
A résumé on a design shows its template's name on the dashboard, as the editor does. Not a bug; listed as remaining.
A font or colour the user set that happens to equal a design's value leaves with the design, the same rule a template's own style follows. By design, and the panel's note says so.

The reviewer checked old data, stale or unknown templatePreset ids, other callers of the changed functions, the exporters, the cover letter, switch_to_classic, contrast and ranges, and found no problem.
